text:
mina: hey team, first day here. VPN connected (our-agent) but `ssh devbox.company` times out. i can ping 10.40.2.15 by IP but hostname doesn't resolve. browser to intranet by name also fails. anyone seen DNS-only issues on linux?

carl: welcome! which distro and are you using NetworkManager/systemd-resolved? paste `ip route` and `resolvectl status` pls.

mina: ubuntu 22.04, GNOME, NetworkManager. paste: 
```
$ ip route
default via 192.168.0.1 dev wlp2s0
10.40.0.0/16 via 172.30.5.1 dev wg0

$ resolvectl status
Global
       Link 2 (wg0)
        Current Scopes: DNS
         LLMNR setting: no
   MulticastDNS setting: no
           DNS Servers: 172.30.5.10
            DNSSEC NTA: 10.in-addr.arpa

Link 3 (wlp2s0)
        Current Scopes: DNS
           DNS Servers: 192.168.0.1
```

mina: so wg0 has the internal DNS but `cat /etc/resolv.conf` points to 127.0.0.53 (systemd stub) and DNS queries go to my router. i can `dig @172.30.5.10 devbox.company` and it returns A record, so DNS works if pointed to the right server.

rita: yep that's common. NetworkManager + systemd-resolved create the stub. When VPN sets WG0 DNS we need systemd-resolved to use it for the host. try `sudo resolvectl dns wg0 172.30.5.10` and `sudo resolvectl domain wg0 ~company` then `resolvectl query devbox.company`. If that works, you can make NetworkManager forwards to systemd-resolved by setting `dns=systemd-resolved` in /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf and restart.

carl: another quick test: `getent hosts devbox.company` vs `nslookup devbox.company`. If getent fails but dig works, it's NSS/systemd stub issue.

mina: ran `sudo resolvectl dns wg0 172.30.5.10` and now `ping devbox.company` resolves and ssh connects. yay. thanks!

mina: is there a persistent fix? i rebooted earlier and it went back to router DNS.

rita: persistent approach: edit /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf add under [main] `dns=systemd-resolved` then `sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager` and `sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf`. On some images we prefer the non-stub `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` so DNS queries go to systemd-resolved which forwards to wg0 DNS. LMK if you want a quick patch i can push for new hires.

carl: filed INFRA-9021 to check fleet image NetworkManager + systemd-resolved defaults; assigned to @rita. infra-bot created ticket.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-9021: "Linux onboarding: systemd-resolved stub prevents VPN DNS from being used for internal names" assigned to @rita. Please attach `resolvectl status` and `journalctl -u NetworkManager` if you hit this again.

mina: okta popped earlier when i first signed in, okta-bot reminded me to finish SSO before VPN. i did that after and then retried. good tip.

okta-bot: Reminder: finish Okta enrollment in your default browser before connecting VPN to ensure policies and DNS pushes are applied.

carl: added a small note to new-hires docs about Linux: if you see IP connectivity but no hostname resolution, check systemd-resolved/NetworkManager and use `resolvectl` to test.

mina: thanks everyone, saved my morning pairing session! :partyparrot:
